clue.text: Life so harassed? Ponder remote part of Scotland

explanation.surface: A harried person decides to think things over somewhere far away in the Scottish wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Mull is a Hebridean island, an outlying and thinly populated piece of Scotland.

clue.text: Gossip had an effect after lawyers upset

past tense of bite in the sense of taking effect, as a new rule bites

explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the effect second, following the overturned lawyers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length, so it serves as a verb meaning gossip.

clue.text: Most of expected lines will be boring

parts.note: a train that is due is expected

explanation.surface: Predictable passages of text will send a reader to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and boring are plain synonyms for something tedious and uninteresting.

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: The prairie dog is a burrowing North American rodent belonging to the squirrel family.

clue.text: Network confusion, according to Connery?

indicators.note: Sean Connery's famous slurred s means we want the word as he would pronounce it

parts.note: confusion is a mess, which Connery's slurred s turns into a different word

explanation.surface: The actor Sean Connery muddles a network of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Sean Connery, the Scottish actor who played James Bond, was known for pronouncing s as sh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh is a net-like web of interlaced threads or wires, that is, a network.

clue.text: Not well and unable to offer entertainments, barring piano

parts.note: a shop that is out of something cannot offer it

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so the letter for the musical term is removed

parts.note: sport in its sense of fun or amusement
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.definitionFit: Out of sorts is an idiom for feeling slightly unwell or below par.

clue.text: Support worker, as seen in court?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but the setting is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhand is a tennis shot played with the back of the hand facing the net, seen on any tennis court.

clue.text: Squad, underpowered, needing boost to energy?

indicators.note: in a down entry a boost lifts the energy letter higher up the column, rearranging the word

parts.note: a tame car or performance lacks power and spirit

explanation.surface: A sluggish sports squad needs more energy to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the symbol for energy, moves up two places in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A team and a squad are both groups of players selected to compete together.

clue.text: Chaotic situation is cool in America, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things backwards, so the combined letters are read right to left

parts.note: abbreviation for the United States
to fan something is to cool it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Is cool' reads as an adjective phrase, but 'is' is only the link and 'cool' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: SNAFU is US military slang (situation normal, all fouled up) for a confused, chaotic mess.

clue.text: Bird expected to throttle feline? Teach again

parts.note: due means expected
a cat is a feline

clue.text: What will secure front of major clock feature is ornament

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast within, so the exclamation encloses the rest

parts.note: the opening letter of major
an alarm clock has a bell
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the link before the definition but it is wordplay; 'will' is the real link.

clue.text: Recycled ropes — used many at first beside tree

parts.note: an oak is a tree

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the two words just before

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Old ropes, reused many times, are tied up next to a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beside' lets the tree come first and the letters follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose fibre picked from old ropes, once used for caulking ships' seams.

clue.text: Obsessive type showing shiftiest moves

indicators.note: when letters move about they change position, giving a rearrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: A fetishist is someone with an obsessive fixation on a particular object or practice.

clue.text: Section governed by young man seizing Northern port

indicators.note: seizing something means grabbing hold of it, so the young man wraps round the letter

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for section
what is governed by someone is under them
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A region ruled by a young man who has grabbed a harbour in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern port' looks like one definition, but 'Northern' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunderland is a port city on the River Wear in north-east England.

clue.text: "Slow-paced": Arab's barbed comment during deal

indicators.note: what happens during something takes place inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: to deal is to trade
Ar. is a dictionary abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
a dig is a pointed remark

explanation.walkthrough: Ar. for Arab is a dictionary abbreviation many solvers will not know; 'slow-paced' is the definition in quotes, a rare adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardigrade is a rare adjective meaning moving slowly, from Latin tardus, slow, and gradi, to walk.

clue.text: Display bear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stall or rack where goods are shown

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal; it is the verb of putting up with something.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand is a display unit for goods, and to stand something is to tolerate or endure it.

clue.text: Unhappiness, note, in pop festival location?

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a marquee where dance music plays at a festival
N is an abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: Grumbling, written down, at the site of a music festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is dissatisfaction, a restless lack of contentment close to unhappiness.

clue.text: Still looking young, suitable for artist's sketching?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a face free of wrinkles
second meaning: plain paper without ruled guidelines

explanation.surface: A youthful-looking person sits for an artist's portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from lines: wrinkles on skin and printed rules on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlined describes a smooth, wrinkle-free face and also blank paper without ruling, ideal for drawing.

clue.text: Float art gallery supporting garment-maker

explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts the gallery underneath the garment-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: To levitate is to rise and hover in the air, which is to float.

clue.text: About to suppress hesitation with computer system for screen in church

DOS is the old disk operating system

clue.text: Historic reception the day before festival, captured in article for Paris Match

indicators.note: something captured in another is held inside it

parts.note: le is a French definite article, as in a magazine like Paris Match
the eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: A period reception held on the eve of a celebration, featured in a French magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris Match is a French weekly magazine; here it just signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee was a morning reception held by a monarch, a court custom of past centuries.

clue.text: Musical effect is smooth, pervading warm feeling? Not entirely

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a slide up or down the scale, a sweeping musical technique.

clue.text: No train service around noon, when I must go? That's commonplace

indicators.note: going around something encloses it
the letter I has to leave, so it is removed

parts.note: taken as written
rail travel is the train service
M for meridies, midday

explanation.walkthrough: Drop the I from NORAIL and slip M inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal is ordinary and usual, which is what commonplace means.

clue.text: African region not found in Gabon at all? Yes and no

surface padding: a wry comment that the region is and is not in Gabon

explanation.walkthrough: 'Yes and no' resolves the riddle: the region is not in Gabon the country, but it is in the words.

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Sarah Bernhardt was the celebrated French stage actress of the late nineteenth century.

clue.text: Rush line in internet program

clue.text: Incline to take in element of basic education?
